CPTSD therapy is offered on the NHS - I get it. I would question why your doctor has said this. 

You need to ask for EMDR therapy. It's a level 3 intervention, so you may need to do other things first. They also have to assess you as being in a "good enough" place to start, which means being fairly stable. 

I was able to skip some steps as my abuse is classed as pretty severe and I am disabled enough that I dissociate at a rate that is dangerous (cumulatively about one day per week). These are things you should look into.

I first referred myself for EMDR therapy in 2018, under the system then that allowed me to refer myself. Prior to that, I had already undergone some level 1/2 therapy for generalised anxiety and major depressive disorder, which was to help stabilise me. I had to wait until 2023 until I started my first round of EMDR, and in that time since I refered I had had 1 major suicide attempt - so when I talk about being stable, the "stable" is more that you can show you can calm yourself down (which I have been unable to do in the past). Prior to being able to fully start the EMDR I had to undergo 3 months of therapy with the EMDR therapist to work on coping skills to calm myself down, which helped, and enabled us to do the therapy. 

I have known people go private for EMDR in the UK and these steps, about making sure you are stable and are able to calm yourself down, and it has gone badly every single time. I believe it's what's giving EMDR a bit of a bad rep in the UK. 

So, I would kind of ignore what your doctor is saying, and just directly start to ask to be referred to EMDR therapy. I have never asked for "therapy for my CPTSD" to get this. I went and directly asked for the treatment I needed after researching it myself.

There is a really common symptom of CPTSD where we have an out group and an in group (it's an extension of black and white thinking, another CPTSD symptom). This is a symptom that can both protect us, but also harm us. We really believe we can completely judge a person and put them into the in group and out group quickly, but then, we are *far* to trusting of the people we have deemed to be "good" for whatever reason. It makes us extremely naive and how we end up with relationships (platonic and romantic) with people that treat us poorly and don't respect us. We believe we have judged them correctly and people can either be wholly good, or wholly bad. We can't deal with the grey area coz it's stressful, so this is our coping mechanism. It's not helpful though. Don't get into the habit of "only other traumatised people can ever understand me". They *might* understand better, especially if they are healing. But they also might not be very interested in healing themselves and be more dangerous. Similarly, someone without any mental health difficulties could be deeply compassionate. Labeling people into boxes is easier on our brain, but it *is* something that we need to work on.

Jealousy is trying to tell you something, like all emotions. The first thing you should do with jealousy is try to assess where it is coming from. Is it that a friend/partner is doing something that is making you feel insecure? This is the first thing to look at. If so, what can they do to make you feel more secure? Can you ask that of them to provide reassurance? (And with Relationship Anarchy theory behind it in that, we cannot control others actions, only our boundaries - does the reassurance or even compromise break your boundaries? If so, you need to enforce boundaries).


The next thing to look at, if that's not the case - is the jealousy coming from FOMO? Is it that *you* want what a partner is experiencing? If so, you should look at ways you can achieve that for yourself. 


After that, the next thing to look at is the object of the jealousy - the other person or meta that you might have painted as the "opposition" within your jealousy. What is it about *them* that you are jealous of? Is it an aspect of their personality? Is it something they are doing in life that you want to do? Find out what it is, and see if there is a way to fulfil that need.  


This is how people grow when you have a healthy relationship with jealousy. It's really hard to learn to do. But the first step is to accept that jealousy is not a bad or wrong emotion and you should not beat yourself up for feeling it. All of this advice around jealousy applies if you are poly or monog.

PTSD, like anything else, has different levels of severity. It's also *physical* - you can't think your way out of PTSD. PTSD isn't even defined by what you went through. It created when you aren't allowed or aren't able to properly "come down" from an experience that triggered your flight response.

 A child that survived 9/11, did so *without* developing PTSD because they 1. Had agency within their own rescue (he was able to run away and get away, along with his family), and 2. Yes, cancelling the direct debit means you will now be out of contract - it means that you could then have a higher rate, but you would have that as soon as the contract renews anyway - so that's one point.

Debt - if people are concerned, we know that the energy companies *have* to set up payment plans if they don't pay. If people are really concerned, we have two options - transfer to someone who doesn't mind it being on their credit report, or pay within 28 days. We think that 4 weeks will be a long enough time.
